title: Passersby
subtitle: A necessary choice in the midst of chance.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Go on, spit it out!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Or have all those long-winded administrative tasks totally destroyed your ability to get to the point?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: You know something, don't you, Adler?
Everyone waits for Enigma to speak, but all they get is a room full of puzzled looks.
No matter how much he despises Constantine's implications and methods, he knows that this is neither the time nor the place for sharing what he's learned.
The words he cannot speak harden into a stone at the back of his throat. Were he to let it fall, the ripples it would send through Laplace would be impossible to calm.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm simply learning to consider the consequences before I act.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Some of the Foundation's committee members have gotten swept up in the prospect of an impending arcane war. If this goes on ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Laplace mustn't become a pawn in their war games, or a bargaining chip for their faction disputes.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: In short, we need to submit our Pre-Storm Protocol as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Which means we need to figure out what the core of the toybox really is—no. Whatever it is, we need to crack it open as soon as possible. Alright?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If we hurry, we still have a chance to convince the talking heads at the Foundation to leave us be.
Each researcher wears a different expression.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Ha, Enigma, are you actually begging right now? Quick—has the "Storm" stopped? Has hell frozen over?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Whatever. Just give me an answer.
The ferrofluid swirls violently in the tank. Then slowly, it settles.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Alright.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: It seems there'll be no solving our differences in the short term.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: So, I have a proposal: we submit two reports and let the reviewers decide.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Fine.
Beach, Toybox
In the toybox once again, Enigma's exploration has taken him to a beach.
Waves roll in, foaming at the shore. He looks down at the swirling water.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: From a visual estimate, the "Perfect Language" covers everything in a five-kilometer radius, with the tower as its center.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: On the beach outside this five-kilometer area, the environment continues to exhibit signs of "language disorder," a new type of Storm Syndrome.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It deconstructs words into phonemes, the building blocks of sound, and uses them as the building blocks of matter. A handful of seawater contains ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: One, two, three, four ... Roughly twenty phonemes.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Though, clearly, the phonemes themselves don't carry any meaning, they do leave room to construct one.
The waves whirl, causing phonemes to clash and ring against one another.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The "waves" create a chiming sound. Like bells.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This "seawater" holds enough phonemes such that they may organize into morphemes, the smallest units of meaning.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hm. Monkeys may have an easier time putting Shakespeare together here than writing it on typewriters.
A jelly-thick sea breeze brushes Enigma's cheek and carries his wry muttering to the waves' crests.
Then the waves break against the shore again, and the wind shifts.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It seems the wind strips even the quietest utterances into the smallest units of sound.
He casts his hearing like a net, carefully sifting out bare phonemes and weaving them back into meaning.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Perhaps these symptoms can be understood as a language microscope. Or maybe a scalpel.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The environment dissolves and dissects every spoken word, leaving only its phonetic fragments behind.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: To use language is to quickly combine these pieces into specific sequences to create a meaningful utterance. Thus, one could view this entire environment as a "simulation of language use."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hmm ... Bilabial plosive, diphthong, mid central vowel, nasal. The phonemes of "poem."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hah. I see, it's encryption and decryption. Hardly foreign territory for me.
Enigma crouches down, pulls a small glass vial from his pocket, and fills it to the two-thirds mark with "seawater."
He seals the vial and shakes it. The liquid inside is crystal-clear.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It still appears like normal seawater in this container. Let's see if X has any suitable equipment to analyze its composition when I get back.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I wonder ... If I bring this vial of "seawater" to the tower, will its "composition" change?
The net catches a few strange symbols.
Not far off, several toybox "locals" rush from the reef in a panic.
Puzzled, Enigma watches as they come running straight toward him, crying all the way.

items.speaker: Piece I
items.text: *%￥—Critter!!
As they draw closer, the phonemes reassemble into words.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This language deconstruction phenomenon seems to have a limited range. Just now the limit was around two meters.
He quickly jots the new finding on the back of his hand, but the locals' shouting robs him of any chance to ponder it further.

items.speaker: Piece I
items.text: Please help us!

items.speaker: Piece I
items.text: Just cross that reef, walk due west, and you'll find it on the shore!
The clamoring callers surround him. No matter which way he steps, they swarm back in an instant.
He tries to convince himself they're nothing but cold data. Not real people. Not worth his time.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Critter attacks are common in the toybox. Go find the fellow with the glass tank for a head.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I need to get to that tower.

items.speaker: Piece I
items.text: Please, please help us! You're the only one here who can!

items.speaker: Piece II
items.text: You'll find a way, won't you?
The pieces refuse to take no for an answer. Their reality has made the choice for them—keep pushing.
Enigma glances down at his timer. Ten hours in the toybox already.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If I waste time on things like this, I won't make any progress on the tower's function before the simulated "Storm" hits.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I need to finish the Pre-Storm Protocol before Ulrich does.

items.speaker: Piece III
items.text: If we wait any longer, our friend will get hurt!

items.speaker: Piece I
items.text: Please help us!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: All the damn pleading—what is this, a time loop?!
When needs collide, the result is either a standoff or a concession, and lately, Enigma has been favoring the latter.
There's not a trace of simulation in the panic on their faces. Not even Laplace's most advanced equipment could reproduce terror so faithfully.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Lead the way.
They cheer and quickly clear a path toward the reef.
On the other side, the "emergency" comes into view: a pack of Critters closing in.

items.speaker: Critter
items.text: [Critter-Speech] (Just you wait!)
It doesn't take much before the Critters flee shrieking.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: Even without understanding their language, and with parts of it reduced to incomprehensible noise, their movements convey their fury just fine.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: Thank you for lending us a hand.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You again.
As he approaches the "trapped survivor," Enigma's eyes fall on a figure before him.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: A simulation of someone he knew better than anyone, built from Greta Hofmann's memory data.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I should've known. This is the only way to the tower.
He mutters under his breath and takes a step forward.
It's a waste of time. None of this is real—just an absurd coincidence generated by the toybox's logic.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I saw you on my previous expeditions.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: Oh, you're from the outside. This world is constantly resetting, so I'm afraid I cannot recall our previous encounters.
But—

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The last time I saw you, you were also on your way to explore the depths of the toybox.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is that the case this time as well?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I built a tower there, in the depths. But nothing has changed.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm no closer to finding out how to stop the "Storm" in here.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Listen to me. This is all a simulation, designed to help us find a solution to the "Storm." No matter what you do, everything will eventually reset to its original state. Nothing will change.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You don't have to waste your time like this. You've already made this journey before, and it is difficult and meaningless.
"Hofmann" studies Enigma calmly. He's standing right in front of her, blocking the road ahead.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: I appreciate your concern. It appears this isn't the first time you've observed our actions.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: And I'm glad I was able to help you come to your conclusions.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: However, everything you've said pertains to your business as an outsider. From your point of view, perhaps your claims are correct.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: But I'll only know if your advice is meaningful to me once I get there myself, when I see that tower with my own eyes.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: In any case, I won't be the last to visit it. Perhaps whatever I leave behind will help those who come after.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: Like I've helped you.

items.speaker: "Hofmann"
items.text: Besides, if you've already concluded that this is meaningless, why did you return?
Leaving the question to hang in the air, "Hofmann" brushes past Enigma and follows the road behind him.
Enigma doesn't move. The timer ticks on, converting precious time into numbers.
A moment later, he sets off down the same road.
